blindSummary:
Male same-sex conduct is criminalised here (up to 2 years under a penal-code provision) and, more fundamentally, this is one of the world's most closed states: the state exerts strict media control and heavy internet monitoring, no independent research on LGBTI issues has been possible since 2019, and asylum is the community's most urgent need, according to a regional LGBTI-rights organisation. An international human-rights organisation has documented systematic abuses. There is no legal gender recognition, no community, no recourse, and no visibility — the only safe strategy is total concealment.

For a visitor: any discoverable online presence or visible nonconformity is dangerous in a state that monitors communications pervasively.
blindOutOfScope: Absence of documentation is itself evidence of severity: data collection is impossible because it is unsafe.
blindSourceSummaries: A regional LGBTI-rights organisation's annual review 2025 (covering 2024), chapter on this country: asylum remains one of the most urgent needs for the LGBTI community; the only documented research on LGBTI issues dates to 2019 (data collection almost impossible due to safety risks); an international human-rights organisation documented systemic discrimination; the April 2022 criminal code retained 'sodomy' provisions and increased the severity and scope of punishments; torture and inhumane treatment by law enforcement reported, with several LGBTI people forced to flee; the state security ministry collaborates with regional AIDS centres, exposing HIV-test data.

A foreign government's 2021 human-rights report on this country: official assessment - same-sex conduct criminalised under the penal-code provision (up to 2 years); societal stigma; the totalitarian state's pervasive repression.

A network of people-living-with-HIV NGOs' mid-term submission to the UN periodic review (2020) on this country: LGBT persons and PLHIV 'have no effective legislative means of enjoying their fundamental human rights'; the penal code criminalises consensual same-sex acts; LGBT persons are increasingly fleeing abroad to seek refuge.

Legal-environment assessment (2019) by an HIV-services NGO with an exile news outlet: legislative analysis related to LGBT rights and HIV in this country - identifies legal barriers for PLHIV, gay men, MSM and trans people, analysing law-enforcement practice and international recommendations.

University law clinic (May 2007): a law school's sexuality-and-gender law clinic secured asylum for a woman from this country who feared persecution because she is a lesbian, in a society where conservative religious norms shape social attitudes.

Law firm (Sept 2019): attorneys secured asylum for a lesbian couple from this country who feared persecution including imprisonment and torture; homosexuality is punishable by up to 2 years; suspects face interrogation, torture and confinement to mental hospitals; women are vulnerable to sexual violence and 'honor killings'.
blindTangential: The penal-code provision criminalising male same-sex conduct (up to 2 years) is a direct risk for trans visitors with partners or perceived as same-sex-active.
